findings.text: `reflect.TypeOf(arg)` returns a nil `reflect.Type` interface when `arg` is nil, so the new `.String()` call panics with a nil pointer dereference. The old `fmt.Sprintf("%s", ...)` printed `%!s(<nil>)` instead. Calling `Arguments{nil, 1}.String()` crashes, and so does a mock assertion or diff-message path that formats arguments containing a nil.
